correctness.rationale: Both displayed seeds occur in sigma^4(0), and generic subsequence dynamic programming gives identical counts for every binary target of length at most 3. The morphism-transfer identity expresses every target count in h(w) as an integer linear combination of source subword counts of lengths at most the target length, so k-binomial equivalence is preserved by morphisms. The period-doubling morphism is injective and uniform, hence all iterates remain distinct factors. Therefore strict third-order binomial versus factor complexity holds at every length 10*2^t. The package independently replays the seed table, eleven iterated levels, and the transfer identity on an exhaustive small test space.
